overview: This 500-page file traces Japanese naval construction and procurement through the 1930s. It combines treaty notifications for individual warships with diplomatic reporting on naval budgets, constitutional disputes, battleship rumors, and the Hiyei controversy. Correspondence also documents American machinery sales, overseas submarine inquiries, fuel purchases, and growing uncertainty about Japan’s secret construction plans.
interest: Vessel-by-vessel treaty notices sit alongside intelligence reports, revealing how American officials tracked Japan’s increasingly secret naval expansion.
